newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises following high March CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises following high March CPI.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar and the currency basket on Wednesday following a higher than expected March consumer price index (CPI), dealers said.
The CPI, released on Tuesday after the setting of the representative rate, posted a 1.0 percent rise. The figure was above analysts' expectations for a 0.7-0.8 percent rise.
"Now it is clear that the Bank of Israel will leave its key lending rate unchanged in the short term and this led to a rise of the shekel," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"The shekel also rose because of the dollar's decline against the mark and yen. The Bank of Israel had to buy almost $100 million to support the basket," he said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for three months.
The Bank of Israel announced on Wednesday that it will maintain the weights of the various currencies that make up the basket to which the shekel is pegged.
Currently, the dollar's weight is 60.1 percent; the Deutsche mark 21.3 percent; the pound sterling 8.2 percent; the French franc 5.1 percent and the yen 5.4 percent.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3980 shekels against 3.4030 on Tuesday. The basket was fixed at 3.6705 shekels against 3.6724 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7005 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.6957 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9704 shekels after 1.9630 on Tuesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3965 shekels.
